notes: The circuit image shows the final single-balloon circuit. The 12 ohm balloon resistor is not drawn in it, so I placed it from the text. It sits on the end of a 2-core speaker cable, and its two cores go into row 6 (the 9V rail row) and row 11 (the transistor collector row). The exact holes (6e and 11a) are assumed.
The two speaker-cable cores are modelled as jumper-wire parts (wire7, wire8), twisted to the resistor leads.

The breadboard image labels rows 1-30 along its length. These map to the catalogue's column numbers, with rows a-e as bank 't' and f-j as bank 'b'. The pushbutton straddles the centre gap: its legs are at e and f in rows 1 and 3.
Left rail: the red (+) strip is tp and the black (-) strip is tn. Any hole number on a rail is the same strip, so the numbers are only approximate positions.

Transistor orientation follows the picture: row 10 is the emitter (wired to ground), row 11 the collector (to the balloon resistor) and row 12 the base (through 330 ohm to GPIO2). The BC635 and the 9V battery snap are new part types.

The Pi GND wire goes to physical pin 6, which I named GND.1, since the catalogue doesn't say which GND port that pin is. The three Pi-to-breadboard wires are pin-to-socket jumpers (jumper-wire-mf). The other three jumpers are pin-to-pin.
The second balloon described in the 'more balloons' section is optional and not drawn in the image, so it is not included.
